title: Temporary top‑up pockets and invoice dispute playbook
creator: Ava Patel
description: Define and implement a controlled mechanism for short‑term capacity top‑ups ("pockets") for Dedicated fleets, plus an operator-facing invoice dispute and reconciliation playbook. The goal is to enable safe, measurable temporary throughput increases without breaking latency SLOs or causing unexpected overage charges for customers. This ticket covers: API and operator controls for issuing pockets, runtime enforcement, metering changes to attribute tokens correctly, billing export adjustments, and the customer invoice dispute workflow.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a light-weight 'topup_pocket' object scoped to a tenant + fleet with duration, max_tps, and accounting_bucket. 2) Runtime: enforce topup via a soft-priority queue that routes excess requests through a limited surge lane on separate capacity where possible. 3) Metering: tag tokens served under a pocket with an accounting label; exports must include pocket_id and effective_rate for reconciliation. 4) Billing: generate a provisional line item flagged as PROVISIONAL_TOPUP; invoices include clear notes and a link to dispute. 5) Operator UI: expose current pockets, remaining headroom, and quick revoke. 6) Add an invoice dispute playbook that maps a customer's claim to metering lines, pocket metadata, and choice of refund/credit/adjustment.
acceptance_criteria: Create API to create/inspect/revoke topup pockets with RBAC guards
Runtime routes < 0.5% of requests through soft-priority lane under steady state; pockets cannot degrade node stability (no OOMs)
Metering exports include pocket_id, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_consumed, and effective_tps
Billing pipeline marks provisional topup line items and attaches reconciliation keys
Operator Console shows pockets with revoke action and a histogram of pocket usage
Runbook documented: steps to validate a customer invoice dispute and issue credit or adjustment
E2E test that creates a pocket, drives traffic, verifies labeled meter lines and a provisional invoice line
rollout_plan: feature-flag backend and API: rollout to internal staging
enable runtime soft-priority lane on canary cluster, monitor OOM/latency for 48h
enable metering tagging in billing-export job and validate test exports
open limited beta to 3 enterprise tenants with sales consent
monitor usage and disputes for 4 weeks, iterate UX and docs
gradual ramp to GA after stakeholders signoff
migration_notes: Existing surge mechanisms will continue to exist; pockets are additive and opt-in per-tenant. Migration for tenants who rely on implicit burst behavior: recommend creating pockets that mirror historical 95th percentile short windows. Billing team must map existing provisional credits to new pocket_id where applicable.
